back: Human effort, physical and mental, used to produce goods and services; its reward is a wage or salary.
Rewards in addition to the wage, such as housing, transport, medical aid, a pension or a company car.
Money rewards of a job: basic pay, overtime, bonuses, commission and expected future earnings.
Features of a job other than pay: conditions, hours, holidays, security, fringe benefits, training, promotion, status, location, job satisfaction.
Skilled: long training and qualifications (engineer). Semi-skilled: some training (machine operator, driver). Unskilled: little or no training (general hand).
Fair wages; job security; health and safety; fringe benefits (also training and promotion).

front: Why might someone accept a lower-paid job?
back: Better non-wage factors: security, pension, safety, regular hours, training, status or being near family.

front: What happens to the wage in a job with dangerous conditions?
back: It tends to be higher: fewer people offer to do the work, so employers must pay more to attract workers.
Overtime pay = overtime hours × basic hourly rate × the overtime multiple (1.5 for time and a half, 2 for double time).
